A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

KDM5A recognizes a 20-mer histone H3 peptide with a preference for the sequence RHRKQ (where R is the methylated lysine) and that the KDM5A binding pocket is large enough to accommodate a variety of histone post-translational modification (PTMs) at the distal epitope, including methylation and acetylation.

the H3 tail is not just a passive substrate for KDM5, but rather a key player in the regulation of KDM5 activity.
